name: FAQ, reader letters
description: An advice column: each question is a short signed reader letter in italics with the reply set below it.

fields.name: intro
fields.label: Intro
fields.default: Every week our shop manager answers the letters, emails and worried notes left at the till of Fern & Fettle, Leeds.

itemFields.name: letter
itemFields.label: Letter
itemFields.default: Is winter a bad time to repot? My rubber plant is climbing out of its pot.

itemFields.name: reply
itemFields.label: Reply
itemFields.default: Wait for March if you can. Roots settle fastest once the plant is growing again.

default.letter: my monstera has not put out a single new leaf since October. Is it sulking, or have I done something wrong?
default.reply: Neither. Most houseplants rest from October to March, when the light drops. Water half as often, skip the feed and expect a new leaf around April.

default.letter: do you deliver? I would love a fiddle-leaf fig, but I do not fancy carrying a tree home on the number 56 bus.
default.reply: We deliver anywhere in Leeds for £6, and free over £60. Tall plants travel upright in our van on Tuesdays and Fridays, and we carry them up the stairs.

default.letter: I live with a cat who eats everything green. Is there anything I can safely keep on a windowsill?
default.reply: Plenty. Calatheas, spider plants, Boston ferns and most herbs are safe for cats. Every pet-safe plant in the shop has a paw sticker on its pot.

default.letter: the peace lily I bought from you in March is already brown at the tips. Can I bring it back?
default.reply: Bring it in. Every plant has a 30-day guarantee, and after that our plant clinic is free on Saturday mornings. Brown tips usually mean hard tap water, which is easy to fix.
